segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yeah, so just to make sure I have the shape right: 45 technician seats, 6 manager seats, and the calibration module for torque and pressure assets. You’re aiming for a June 3 go-live, correct?

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That’s right. We have 51 users total. The big thing is we need the reminders running before our June audit, which starts June 17.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Makes sense. For that seat count, the annual subscription is $38,400, and implementation is a one-time $6,200. That includes the data import for up to 8,000 instruments and two admin training sessions.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Okay. We’ve got about 6,700 instruments today, so that fits. On billing, can you invoice the subscription now and the implementation after kickoff?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yes, we can split it that way. Subscription invoice on signature, implementation invoice on the May 13 kickoff date. Net 30 on both, unless you need net 45 for AP.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Net 30 is fine. Procurement will ask about the term. Is it a straight 12 months?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Yep, 12 months, June 3, 2026 through June 2, 2027. Renewal is annual, and we’ll reach out 90 days before the end of term to review seats and usage.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Good. We may add the dimensional team later, maybe another 12 seats in Q4. Do we have to redo the whole agreement?

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: No, you can add seats mid-term. They’d be prorated to the June 2 end date, same per-seat rate as this order.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: That works. Send me the order form and I’ll route it today. If legal doesn’t change anything, I think we can sign by Friday.

segments.speaker: Rep
segments.text: Perfect. I’ll send the order form with the pricing, billing split, June 3 start date, and the implementation scope in one packet this afternoon.

segments.speaker: Customer
segments.text: Great. Copy Jenna in procurement and Mark from quality, please. They’ll both want to see it.
